class_comments.dbo:Abbey: An abbey is a Catholic monastery or convent, under the authority of an Abbot or an Abbess, who serves as the spiritual father or mother of the community.
class_comments.dbo:AcademicJournal: An academic journal is a mostly peer-reviewed periodical in which scholarship relating to a particular academic discipline is published. Academic journals serve as forums for the introduction and presentation for scrutiny of new research, and the critique of existing research. Content typically takes the form of articles presenting original research, review articles, and book reviews.
class_comments.dbo:AcademicSubject: Genres of art, e.g. Mathematics, History, Philosophy, Medicine
class_comments.dbo:Actor: An actor or actress is a person who acts in a dramatic production and who works in film, television, theatre, or radio in that capacity.
class_comments.dbo:AdministrativeRegion: A PopulatedPlace under the jurisdiction of an administrative body. This body may administer either a whole region or one or more adjacent Settlements (town administration)
class_comments.dbo:AdultActor: A pornographic actor or actress or a porn star is a person who performs sex acts in film, normally characterised as a pornographic film.
class_comments.dbo:Agent: Analogous to a foaf:Agent, an agent is an entity that acts. This is intended to be the super class of Person and Organisation.
class_comments.dbo:Ambassador: An ambassador is the highest ranking diplomat that represents a nation and is usually accredited to a foreign sovereign or government, or to an international organization.
class_comments.dbo:AmericanFootballLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in american football.
class_comments.dbo:Anime: A style of animation originating in Japan
class_comments.dbo:ArchitecturalStructure: An architectural structure is a human-made, free-standing, immobile outdoor construction (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architectural_structure).
class_comments.dbo:Archive: Collection of documents pertaining to a person or organisation.
class_comments.dbo:Area: Area of something. Use "value" for the value, "min" & "max" for a range (if uncertain) and "rank" (integer) for the rank of that thing amongst its siblings (eg regions ordered by area)
class_comments.dbo:Arena: An arena is an enclosed area, often circular or oval-shaped, designed to showcase theater, musical performances, or sporting events. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena)
class_comments.dbo:Arrondissement: An administrative (France) or lawcourts (Netherlands) body governing a territorial unity on the intermediate level, between local and national level
class_comments.dbo:ArtificialSatellite: In the context of spaceflight, an artificial satellite is an artificial object which has been intentionally placed into orbit.
class_comments.dbo:ArtisticGenre: Genres of art, e.g. Pointillist, Modernist
class_comments.dbo:Artwork: A work of art, artwork, art piece, or art object is an aesthetic item or artistic creation.
class_comments.dbo:Attack: An Attack is not necessarily part of a Military Conflict
class_comments.dbo:AustralianFootballLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in australian football.
class_comments.dbo:AutoRacingLeague: a group of sports teams or individual athletes that compete against each other in auto racing
class_comments.dbo:Bank: a company which main services are banking or financial services.
class_comments.dbo:BaseballLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Baseball.
class_comments.dbo:BasketballLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Basketball
class_comments.dbo:Beach: The shore of a body of water, especially when sandy or pebbly.
class_comments.dbo:Beverage: A drink, or beverage, is a liquid which is specifically prepared for human consumption.
class_comments.dbo:Birth: someone's birth as a type of personal event
class_comments.dbo:BowlingLeague: a group of sports teams or players that compete against each other in Bowling
class_comments.dbo:BoxingLeague: A group of sports teams or fighters that compete against each other in Boxing
class_comments.dbo:Bridge: A bridge is a structure built to span physical obstacles such as a body of water, valley, or road, for the purpose of providing passage over the obstacle (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge).
class_comments.dbo:BroadcastNetwork: A broadcast network is an organization, such as a corporation or other association, that provides live or recorded content, such as movies, newscasts, sports, and public affairs programs for broadcast over a group of radio or television stations. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_network - 28/03/2011)
class_comments.dbo:Broadcaster: A broadcaster is an organisation responsible for the production of radio or television programs and/or their transmission. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcaster - 28/03/2011)
class_comments.dbo:Building: Building is defined as a Civil Engineering structure such as a house, worship center, factory etc. that has a foundation, wall, roof etc. that protect human being and their properties from direct harsh effect of weather like rain, wind, sun etc. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Building).
class_comments.dbo:CanadianFootballLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in canadian football league.
class_comments.dbo:Canton: An administrative (France) or lawcourts (Netherlands) body governing a territorial unity on the municipal level or somewhat above
class_comments.dbo:Capital: A municipality enjoying primary status in a state, country, province, or other region as its seat of government.
class_comments.dbo:CapitalOfRegion: seat of a first order administration division.
class_comments.dbo:CardinalDirection: One of the four main directions on a compass or any other system to determine a geographical position
class_comments.dbo:CareerStation: this class marks a career step in the life of a person, e.g. a soccer player, holding information on the time span, matches and goals he or she achieved at a certain club
class_comments.dbo:Case: A case is the total of work done to prepare for an administrative or business decision. As a rule, a case is reflected in a set of documents.
class_comments.dbo:Casino: In modern English, a casino is a facility which houses and accommodates certain types of gambling activities.
class_comments.dbo:Castle: Castles often are, but need not be a military structure. They can serve for status, pleasure and hunt as well.
class_comments.dbo:Cheese: A milk product prepared for human consumption
class_comments.dbo:Chef: a person who cooks professionally for other people
class_comments.dbo:ChristianDoctrine: Tenets of the Christian faith, e.g. Trinity, Nicene Creed
class_comments.dbo:Church: This is used for church buildings, not any other meaning of church.
class_comments.dbo:City: a relatively large and permanent settlement, particularly a large urban settlement
class_comments.dbo:CityDistrict: District, borough, area or neighbourhood in a city or town
class_comments.dbo:ClericalAdministrativeRegion: An administrative body governing some territorial unity, in this case a clerical administrative body
class_comments.dbo:CoalPit: A coal pit is a place where charcoal is or was extracted
class_comments.dbo:CollectionOfValuables: Collection of valuables is a collection considered to be a work in itself)
class_comments.dbo:Colour: Color or colour is the visual perceptual property corresponding in humans to the categories called red, yellow, blue and others. Color derives from the spectrum of light (distribution of light energy versus wavelength) interacting in the eye with the spectral sensitivities of the light receptors.
class_comments.dbo:ConcentrationCamp:
camp in which people are imprisoned or confined, commonly in large groups, without trial.
Includes concentration, extermination, transit, detention, internment, (forced) labor, prisoner-of-war, Gulag; Nazi camps related to the Holocaust
class_comments.dbo:ControlledDesignationOfOriginWine: A quality assurance label for wines
class_comments.dbo:CountrySeat: A country seat is a rural patch of land owned by a land owner.
class_comments.dbo:Creek: the portion of a stream that is affected by ebb and flow of ocean tides
class_comments.dbo:CricketLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Cricket
class_comments.dbo:CultivatedVariety: A cultivar is a plant or grouping of plants selected for desirable characteristics that can be maintained by propagation. A plant whose origin or selection is primarily due to intentional human activity.
class_comments.dbo:CurlingLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Curling
class_comments.dbo:CyclingLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Cycling
class_comments.dbo:Dam: A dam is part of a landscape infrastructure, like waterworks (canals) or roads, much more than a building, though, of course, it has been built, too.
class_comments.dbo:Deanery: The intermediate level of a clerical administrative body between parish and diocese
class_comments.dbo:Death: someone's death as a type of personal event
class_comments.dbo:Decoration: An object, such as a medal or an order, that is awarded to honor the recipient ostentatiously.
class_comments.dbo:Demographics: Population of a place. Uses these properties: populationTotal, year (when measured, populationYear), rank (sortOrder of this place amongst its siblings at the same level), name (areal measured by the population, eg: "locality", "municipality" or "comitat")
class_comments.dbo:Desert: A barren area of land where little precipitation occurs.
class_comments.dbo:Dike: A dike is an elongated naturally occurring ridge or artificially constructed fill or wall, which regulates water levels
class_comments.dbo:Diocese: District or see under the supervision of a bishop.
class_comments.dbo:DistrictWaterBoard: Conservancy, governmental agency dedicated to surface water management
class_comments.dbo:Divorce: two people's divorce as a type of personal event
class_comments.dbo:Earthquake: the result of a sudden release of energy in the Earth's crust that creates seismic waves
class_comments.dbo:Economist: An economist is a professional in the social science discipline of economics.
class_comments.dbo:Employer: a person, business, firm, etc, that employs workers.
class_comments.dbo:EmployersOrganisation: An employers' organisation is an organisation of entrepreneurs who work together to coordinate their actions in the field of labour relations
class_comments.dbo:Factory: A factory (previously manufactory) or manufacturing plant is an industrial site, usually consisting of buildings and machinery, or more commonly a complex having several buildings, where workers manufacture goods or operate machines processing one product into another.
class_comments.dbo:Family: A group of people related by common descent, a lineage.
class_comments.dbo:Fashion: type or code of dressing, according to the standards of the time or individual design.
class_comments.dbo:Fiefdom: The territory under the authority of a feudal lord
class_comments.dbo:FieldHockeyLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Field Hockey
class_comments.dbo:Food: Food is any eatable or drinkable substance that is normally consumed by humans.
class_comments.dbo:FootballMatch: a competition between two football teams
class_comments.dbo:Forest: A natural place more or less densely grown with trees
class_comments.dbo:FormerMunicipality: A municipality that has ceased to exist, and most of the time got incorporated (wholesale or partly) into another municipality
class_comments.dbo:Fort: Fortified place, most of the time to protect traffic routes
class_comments.dbo:Game: a structured activity, usually undertaken for enjoyment and sometimes used as an educational tool
class_comments.dbo:Garden: A garden is a planned space, usually outdoors, set aside for the display, cultivation, and enjoyment of plants and other forms of nature. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden)
class_comments.dbo:Gate: Gate is defined as a built structure marking the entrance to a building or an estate.
class_comments.dbo:GolfLeague: Golfplayer that compete against each other in Golf
class_comments.dbo:GovernmentAgency: A government agency is a permanent or semi-permanent organization in the machinery of government that is responsible for the oversight and administration of specific functions, such as an intelligence agency.
class_comments.dbo:GovernmentCabinet: A cabinet is a body of high-ranking state officials, typically consisting of the top leaders of the executive branch.
class_comments.dbo:GovernmentalAdministrativeRegion: An administrative body governing some territorial unity, in this case a governmental administrative body
class_comments.dbo:GraveMonument: A monument erected on a tomb, or a memorial stone.
class_comments.dbo:Gymnast: A gymnast is one who performs gymnastics
class_comments.dbo:HandballLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Handball
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalAreaOfAuthority: Mostly for feudal forms of authority, but can also serve for historical forms of centralised authority
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalCountry: A place which used to be a country.
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalDistrict: a place which used to be a district.
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalPeriod: A historical Period should be linked to a Place by way of the property dct:spatial (already defined)
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalProvince: A place which used to be a province.
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalRegion: a place which used to be a region.
class_comments.dbo:HistoricalSettlement: A place which used to be a city or town or village.
class_comments.dbo:Hormone: A hormone is any member of a class of signaling molecules produced by glands in multicellular organisms that are transported by the circulatory system to target distant organs to regulate physiology and behaviour.
class_comments.dbo:IceHockeyLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Ice Hockey.
class_comments.dbo:Image: A document that contains a visual image
class_comments.dbo:InformationAppliance: An information device such as PDAs or Video game consoles, etc.
class_comments.dbo:InlineHockeyLeague: group of sports teams that compete against each other in Inline Hockey.
class_comments.dbo:InternationalOrganisation: An international organisation is either a private or a public organisation seeking to accomplish goals across country borders
class_comments.dbo:LacrosseLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Lacrosse.
class_comments.dbo:LawFirm: A law firm is a business entity formed by one or more lawyers to engage in the practice of law. The primary service provided by a law firm is to advise clients (individuals or corporations) about their legal rights and responsibilities, and to represent their clients in civil or criminal cases, business transactions, and other matters in which legal advice and other assistance are sought.
class_comments.dbo:Lawyer: a person who is practicing law.
class_comments.dbo:LineOfFashion: A coherent type of clothing or dressing following a particular fashion
class_comments.dbo:LiteraryGenre: Genres of literature, e.g. Satire, Gothic
class_comments.dbo:Magazine: Magazines, periodicals, glossies or serials are publications, generally published on a regular schedule, containing a variety of articles. They are generally financed by advertising, by a purchase price, by pre-paid magazine subscriptions, or all three.
class_comments.dbo:Manga: Manga are comics created in Japan
class_comments.dbo:Manhwa: Korean term for comics and print cartoons
class_comments.dbo:Marriage: someone's marriage as a type of personal event
class_comments.dbo:MathematicalConcept: Mathematical concepts, e.g. Fibonacci numbers, Imaginary numbers, Symmetry
class_comments.dbo:Media: storage and transmission channels or tools used to store and deliver information or data
class_comments.dbo:Medicine: The science and art of healing the human body and identifying the causes of disease
class_comments.dbo:Meeting: A regular or irregular meeting of people as an event to keep record of
class_comments.dbo:Memorial: A monument erected to commemorate a person, an event and/or group. In the case of a person, this might be a grave or tomb.
class_comments.dbo:MicroRegion: A microregion is a - mainy statistical - region in Brazil, at an administrative level between a meso-region and a community
class_comments.dbo:MilitaryStructure: A military structure such as a Castle, Fortress, Wall, etc.
class_comments.dbo:Mill: a unit operation designed to break a solid material into smaller pieces
class_comments.dbo:Mine: A mine is a place where mineral resources are or were extracted
class_comments.dbo:Mineral: A naturally occurring solid chemical substance.
class_comments.dbo:MixedMartialArtsLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Mixed Martial Arts
class_comments.dbo:Monastery: Monastery denotes the building, or complex of buildings, comprising the domestic quarters and workplace(s) of monastics, whether monks or nuns, and whether living in community or alone (hermits). The monastery generally includes a place reserved for prayer which may be a chapel, church or temple, and may also serve as an oratory.
class_comments.dbo:Monument: A type of structure (a statue or an art object) created to commemorate a person or important event, not necessarily of a catastrophic nature.
class_comments.dbo:Mosque: A mosque, sometimes spelt mosk, is a place of worship for followers of Islam.
class_comments.dbo:MotorcycleRacingLeague: a group of sports teams or bikerider that compete against each other in Motorcycle Racing
class_comments.dbo:MountainPass: a path that allows the crossing of a mountain chain. It is usually a saddle point in between two areas of higher elevation
class_comments.dbo:MountainRange: a chain of mountains bordered by highlands or separated from other mountains by passes or valleys.
class_comments.dbo:MovieDirector: a person who oversees making of film.
class_comments.dbo:MovingImage: A visual document that is intended to be animated; equivalent to http://purl.org/dc/dcmitype/MovingImage
class_comments.dbo:Municipality: An administrative body governing a territorial unity on the lower level, administering one or a few more settlements
class_comments.dbo:MusicDirector: A person who is the director of an orchestra or concert band.
class_comments.dbo:NationalAnthem: Patriotic musical composition which is the offcial national song.
class_comments.dbo:NaturalPlace: The natural place encompasses all places occurring naturally in universe.
class_comments.dbo:Newspaper: A newspaper is a regularly scheduled publication containing news of current events, informative articles, diverse features and advertising. It usually is printed on relatively inexpensive, low-grade paper such as newsprint.
class_comments.dbo:NobleFamily: Family deemed to be of noble descent
class_comments.dbo:Novel: A book of long narrative in literary prose
class_comments.dbo:Ocean: A body of saline water that composes much of a planet's hydrosphere.
class_comments.dbo:Organ: All types and sizes of organs
class_comments.dbo:PaintballLeague: a group of sports teams that compete against each other in Paintball
class_comments.dbo:Painting: Describes a painting to assign picture entries in wikipedia to artists.
class_comments.dbo:Parish: The smallest unit of a clerical administrative body
class_comments.dbo:Park: A park is an area of open space provided for recreational use. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park
class_comments.dbo:PeriodicalLiterature: Periodical literature (also called a periodical publication or simply a periodical) is a published work that appears in a new edition on a regular schedule. The most familiar examples are the newspaper, often published daily, or weekly; or the magazine, typically published weekly, monthly or as a quarterly. Other examples would be a newsletter, a literary journal or learned journal, or a yearbook.
class_comments.dbo:PersonalEvent: an event that occurs in someone's personal life
class_comments.dbo:PhilosophicalConcept: Philosophical concepts, e.g. Existentialism, Cogito Ergo Sum
class_comments.dbo:Play: A play is a form of literature written by a playwright, usually consisting of scripted dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance rather than just reading.
class_comments.dbo:PlayWright: A person who writes dramatic literature or drama.
class_comments.dbo:PoloLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in Polo.
class_comments.dbo:PopulatedPlace: As defined by the United States Geological Survey, a populated place is a place or area with clustered or scattered buildings and a permanent human population (city, settlement, town, or village) referenced with geographic coordinates (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populated_place).
class_comments.dbo:Port: a location on a coast or shore containing one or more harbors where ships can dock and transfer people or cargo to or from land.
class_comments.dbo:Producer: a person who manages movies or music recordings.
class_comments.dbo:Project: A project is a temporary endeavor undertaken to achieve defined objectives.
class_comments.dbo:ProtectedArea: This class should be used for protected nature. For enclosed neighbourhoods there is now class GatedCommunity
class_comments.dbo:Province: An administrative body governing a territorial unity on the intermediate level, between local and national level
class_comments.dbo:PublicTransitSystem: A public transit system is a shared passenger transportation service which is available for use by the general public. Public transport modes include buses, trolleybuses, trams and trains, 'rapid transit' (metro/subways/undergrounds etc) and ferries. Intercity public transport is dominated by airlines, coaches, and intercity rail. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_transit).
class_comments.dbo:Pyramid: a structure whose shape is roughly that of a pyramid in the geometric sense.
class_comments.dbo:Racecourse: A racecourse is an alternate term for a horse racing track, found in countries such as the United Kingdom, Australia, Hong Kong, and the United Arab Emirates.
class_comments.dbo:RadioControlledRacingLeague: A group of sports teams or person that compete against each other in radio-controlled racing.
class_comments.dbo:RadioStation: A radio station has one line up. For instance the radio station BBC Radio 1. Not to be confused with the broadcasting network BBC, which has many radio stations.
class_comments.dbo:RailwayLine: A railway line is a transport service by trains that pull passengers or freight provided by an organization. Not to be mistaken for railway track, which is the structure consisting of the rails. Wikipedia do not clearly differentiate between both, so there is one infobox describing tracks and lines.
class_comments.dbo:Referee: An official who watches a game or match closely to ensure that the rules are adhered to.
class_comments.dbo:Reference: Reference to a work (book, movie, website)  providing info about the subject
class_comments.dbo:ResearchProject: A research project is a scientific investigation, usually using scientific methods, to achieve defined objectives.
class_comments.dbo:RestArea: A rest area is part of a Road, meant to stop and rest. More often than not, there is a filling station
class_comments.dbo:Resume: A Resume describes a persons work experience and skill set.
class_comments.dbo:RoadJunction: A road junction is a location where vehicular traffic going in different directions can proceed in a controlled manner designed to minimize accidents. In some cases, vehicles can change between different routes or directions of travel (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_%28road%29).
class_comments.dbo:RouteOfTransportation: A route of transportation (thoroughfare) may refer to a public road, highway, path or trail or a route on water from one place to another for use by a variety of general traffic (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughfare).
class_comments.dbo:RouteStop: one stage or stop on a road.
class_comments.dbo:RugbyLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in rugby.
class_comments.dbo:Satellite: An astronomic object orbiting around a planet or star. Definition partly derived from http://www.ontotext.com/proton/protonext# (and thus WordNet 1.7).
class_comments.dbo:ScientificConcept: Scientific concepts, e.g. Theory of relativity, Quantum gravity
class_comments.dbo:Sculpture: Sculpture is three-dimensional artwork created by shaping or combining hard materials, typically stone such as marble, metal, glass, or wood, or plastic materials such as clay, textiles, polymers and softer metals.
class_comments.dbo:Single: In music, a single or record single is a type of release, typically a recording of fewer tracks than an LP or a CD.
class_comments.dbo:SiteOfSpecialScientificInterest: A Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) is a conservation designation denoting a protected area in the United Kingdom. SSSIs are the basic building block of site-based nature conservation legislation and most other legal nature/geological conservation designations in Great Britain are based upon them, including National Nature Reserves, Ramsar Sites, Special Protection Areas, and Special Areas of Conservation.
class_comments.dbo:SnookerChamp: An athlete that plays snooker and won the world championship at least once
class_comments.dbo:SnookerPlayer: An athlete that plays snooker, which is a billard derivate
class_comments.dbo:SnookerWorldRanking: The official world ranking in snooker for a certain year/season
class_comments.dbo:Soccer: A sports game in which the ball must be played by foot
class_comments.dbo:SoccerLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in soccer.
class_comments.dbo:SocietalEvent: an event that is clearly different from strictly personal events
class_comments.dbo:SoftballLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in softball.
class_comments.dbo:Sound: An audio document intended to be listened to; equivalent to http://purl.org/dc/dcmitype/Sound
class_comments.dbo:SpeedwayLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in motorcycle speedway racing.
class_comments.dbo:Sport: A sport is commonly defined as an organized, competitive, and skillful physical activity.
class_comments.dbo:SportsEvent: a event of competitive physical activity
class_comments.dbo:SportsLeague: A group of sports teams or individual athletes that compete against each other in a specific sport.
class_comments.dbo:SportsManager: According to the french label sub Soccer, trainership could be meant. However, here a Sportsmanager is interpreted as a member of the board of a sporting club.
class_comments.dbo:SportsTeamMember: A member of an athletic team.
class_comments.dbo:SportsTeamSeason: A season for a particular sports team (as opposed to the season for the entire league that the team is in)
class_comments.dbo:StatedResolution: A Resolution describes a formal statement adopted by a meeting or convention.
class_comments.dbo:Station: Public transport station (eg. railway station, metro station, bus station).
class_comments.dbo:StillImage: A visual document that is not intended to be animated; equivalent to http://purl.org/dc/dcmitype/StillImage
class_comments.dbo:Stream: a flowing body of water with a current, confined within a bed and stream banks
class_comments.dbo:Street: A Street is different from a Road in as far as the infrastructure aspect is much less important here. A Street is a social and architectural ensemble much more than the connection between two geographic points.
class_comments.dbo:SubMunicipality: An administrative body governing a territorial unity on the lowest level, administering part of a municipality
class_comments.dbo:Swimmer: a trained athlete who participates in swimming meets
class_comments.dbo:Synagogue: A synagogue, sometimes spelt synagog, is a Jewish or Samaritan house of prayer.
class_comments.dbo:SystemOfLaw: a system of legislation, either national or international
class_comments.dbo:Taxon: a category within a classification system for Species
class_comments.dbo:TeamMember: A member of an athletic team.
class_comments.dbo:TeamSport: A team sport is commonly defined as a sport that is being played by competing teams
class_comments.dbo:TelevisionDirector: a person who directs the activities involved in making a television program.
class_comments.dbo:TelevisionEpisode: A television episode is a part of serial television program.
class_comments.dbo:TelevisionStation: A television station has usually one line up. For instance the television station WABC-TV (or ABC 7, Channel 7). Not to be confused with the broadcasting network ABC, which has many television stations.
class_comments.dbo:TennisLeague: A group of sports teams or person that compete against each other in tennis.
class_comments.dbo:Territory: A territory may refer to a country subdivision, a non-sovereign geographic region.
class_comments.dbo:Theatre: A theater or theatre (also a playhouse) is a structure where theatrical works or plays are performed or other performances such as musical concerts may be produced.
class_comments.dbo:TheatreDirector: A director in the theatre field who oversees and orchestrates the mounting of a theatre production.
class_comments.dbo:TheologicalConcept: Theological concepts, e.g. The apocalypse, Trinty, Stoicism
class_comments.dbo:Tower: A Tower is a kind of structure (not necessarily a building) that is higher than the rest
class_comments.dbo:Town: a settlement ranging from a few hundred to several thousand (occasionally hundreds of thousands). The precise meaning varies between countries and is not always a matter of legal definition. Usually, a town is thought of as larger than a village but smaller than a city, though there are exceptions to this rule.
class_comments.dbo:TrackList: A list of music tracks, like on a CD
class_comments.dbo:TradeUnion: A trade union or labor union is an organization of workers who have banded together to achieve common goals such as better working conditions.
class_comments.dbo:Treadmill: A mill driven by the tractive power of horses, donkeys or even people
class_comments.dbo:Tunnel: A tunnel may be for foot or vehicular road traffic, for rail traffic, or for a canal. Some tunnels are aqueducts to supply water for consumption or for hydroelectric stations or are sewers (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel).
class_comments.dbo:Type: a category within a classification system
class_comments.dbo:UndergroundJournal: An underground journal is, although over time there have always been publications forbidden by law, a phenomenon typical of countries occupied by the Germans during the Second World War. The writing in the underground press aims at stiffening a spirit of resistance against Nazi occupation. The distribution of underground journals had to be very secretive and was, therefore, very much dependant on illegal distribution circuits and the hazards of persecution by the occupant.
class_comments.dbo:UnitOfWork: This class is meant to convey the notion of an amount work to be done. It is different from Activity in that it has a definite end and is being measured.
class_comments.dbo:Valley: a depression with predominant extent in one direction
class_comments.dbo:VideoGame: A video game is an electronic game that involves interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device.
class_comments.dbo:VideogamesLeague: A group of sports teams or person that compete against each other in videogames.
class_comments.dbo:Village: a clustered human settlement or community, usually smaller a town
class_comments.dbo:Volcano: A volcano is currently subclass of naturalplace, but it might also be considered a mountain.
class_comments.dbo:VolleyballLeague: A group of sports teams that compete against each other in volleyball.
class_comments.dbo:WaterTower: a construction designed to store larger quantities of water at a place of some elevation in order to keep pressure on the water provision system
class_comments.dbo:Watermill: A watermill is a structure that uses a water wheel or turbine to drive a mechanical process such as flour, lumber or textile production, or metal shaping (rolling, grinding or wire drawing)
class_comments.dbo:WindMotor: A wind-driven turbine that adapts itself to wind direction and to wind-force. Is considered to be a class in its own, despite the wind as common factor with Windmill.
class_comments.dbo:Windmill: A windmill is a machine that converts the energy of wind into rotational energy by means of vanes called sails
class_comments.dbo:WorldHeritageSite: A UNESCO World Heritage Site is a site (such as a forest, mountain, lake, desert, monument, building, complex, or city) that is on the list that is maintained by the international World Heritage Programme administered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee, composed of 21 state parties which are elected by their General Assembly for a four-year term. A World Heritage Site is a place of either cultural or physical significance.
class_comments.dbo:WrittenWork: Written work is any text written to read it (e.g.: books, newspaper, articles)
